errors.description: Pixel-diffing regular-collar-20.jpg against square-in-65cm.jpg isolates a 178px cluster at x=66-89 / y=112-140 on the LEFT leaf. Enlarged 20x it resolves as a triangle with its apex up at (80,112), a short vertical bar inside from (78,122) to (79,129), and a BOLD FLAT HORIZONTAL BASE at y=130 running x=69 to 86 (about 17px) at which the left leaf's outer edge STOPS - about 7px above where the right leaf's tip falls at (133,139.5) - with the small circle at (76.5,135.5) sitting BELOW that flat edge. The candidate instead renders a normally pointed left leaf, equal in length to the right, with the triangle applied as surface topstitching across its face and the button on the leaf.
errors.expected: Left leaf terminating at a straight horizontal edge with the triangular element above it and the small round button below that edge - most consistent with the left point being drawn TURNED BACK to expose its underside and stay pocket, the button on the shirt body showing beneath
errors.actual: Left leaf drawn full-length and pointed like the right, triangle as flat stitching on the leaf face, button on the leaf
errors.correction: Render the left collar point folded back on itself along a straight horizontal fold, so the underside of the point faces the camera as a triangular panel with the collar stay visible as a slim vertical bar in its pocket, and the shirt-body button exposed on the placket just below the fold, while the right point stays down and buttoned.

notes:
Every named defect is fixed: staging is frontal, the 80 degrees reads at 81.2, and both the triangular leaf element and the leaf buttons are present.

THIS OPTION IS THE CONTROL CASE FOR THE PRINTED-CALLOUT FINDING. Its correction was the only one in the set that carried the number '80 degrees' into the prompt, and it is the only one that landed on its printed angle - 81.2 against 80.00. The four whose prompts carried no angle drifted to 71, 84, 89 and 70 against printed 60/80/80/80.

SPEC-VERSUS-DRAWING: the label and description call this a plain 'moderately spread everyday collar (pattern #20)' with no mention of buttons or stays, while the drawing carries two tip buttons and a triangular stay/turn-back element. The drawing wins and the render followed it.

NOT settled at 229px: whether that triangle is a turned-back left point revealing its stay pocket, or a see-through callout on a normal leaf. The bold flat base at y=130 and the button falling below it favour the turned-back reading, but it is not certain and no figure was invented for it.

CROSS-OPTION RISK TO RECORD: this drawing and square-in-65cm-with-button.jpg print the same 80.00 degrees and both carry tip buttons, so in the ILLUSTRATIONS the triangle is the ONLY thing separating them. The two renders are currently separable mainly because sq-65-btn came out 11 degrees narrow; once that is corrected, distinguishability rests entirely on this faint triangle.
